facets.answer: NVIDIA reported shipping initial Vera Rubin samples to customers in February 2026. Management later guided to production shipments beginning in Q3 2026, within the second half. This supports customer sampling and a stated production schedule, not proof that production or commercial-scale shipments have begun or continued. A third-party claim of full production is not accompanied by shipment results and does not resolve that gap. Possible supply-chain or geopolitical delays remain a risk, not a confirmed delay.

The strongest realized customer milestone is CoreWeave’s June bring-up and validation of Vera Rubin NVL72. That establishes technical readiness with a customer, but not a production deployment or operating service. Other signals—including planned 2027 SK Telecom facilities, SpaceX’s planned satellite payload, and reported cloud-provider sign-ups—are prospective commitments or plans. The card does not establish that customers have put Vera Rubin into production use.

The card provides no Vera-specific realized revenue figure. NVIDIA’s nearly $20 billion annual standalone CPU revenue figure is guidance, not an actual result, and should not be treated as total Vera Rubin system revenue. Verification is also limited by the lack of separate reported Vera revenue; supply readiness and customer commitments do not establish recognized sales.
